attrs.evidence: R5.2 closed eleven incidents with two strings, `fixed_by` and `refused_by`, and executed neither. GPT-5.6's attack D retargeted one at "check-mosaic.mjs §99, which does not exist" and the gate stayed green. All eleven closures were in fact real, which is what made the mechanism invisible: nothing had ever been wrong, so nothing had ever surfaced. §5b now runs every registered mutation on every invocation; §8 refuses any closure naming a mutation that did not run. The positive control is not decoration — without it a predicate that refuses everything would close every incident in the registry, which is the same defect as a gate that accepts everything and is harder to see.
attrs.implementation_binding: scripts/check-mosaic.mjs — P.incidentClosure and the §5b mutation harness
attrs.prior_art: Mutation testing, applied to an assurance registry rather than to a test suite. Fable R5.2 F4; GPT-5.6 accept/implement.
attrs.statement: An incident is closed if and only if its registered reproducer mutation is applied to a copy of the registries in the current run and observed to be refused, AND a positive control confirms the same predicate accepts the unmutated tree. `refused_by` is retired.
